neighbours.label: the preposition that ties a harm or effect to its cause or target: 'reaction after vaccination', 'effect on the economy', 'risk for cancer'
fire: Several children developed a high fever after the second injection.
Economists expect the strike to have a severe impact on tourism.
Workers near the plant face a higher risk for lung disease.
Some people get a headache after drinking red wine.
The drought had a devastating effect on the wheat harvest.
Patients reported dizziness after starting the new medication.
Rising rates put heavy pressure on small businesses.
Smokers carry an increased risk for heart attacks.
quiet: Several children went home early after the second lesson.
Economists expect the festival to bring visitors on the weekend.
Workers near the plant face a long drive for lunch.
Some people take a walk after drinking their morning coffee.
The farmers had a long meeting on the wheat harvest.
Patients filled in a form after starting the new program.
The bakery put fresh bread on the shelves.
Smokers gathered outside for a chat after work.

notes: card: ' after' x4, ' over' x4, ' on' x3, ' risk(s)' x5 in adverse-effect contexts; probe: 'rash after vaccination' 0.62 vs 'after lunch' 0.07, 'effect on exports' 0.35. Near misses keep the same prepositions in neutral contexts.
